title: Algebraic closure in a finitely generated field extension is finite
statement: Let $K/k$ be a finitely generated field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $k_{\mathrm{alg}}\subseteq K$ be the algebraic closure of $k$ in $K$, namely the subfield of elements of $K$ algebraic over $k$ [def-weil-relative-algebraic-closure]. Then $k_{\mathrm{alg}}/k$ is finite: $[k_{\mathrm{alg}}:k]<\infty$.

proof.text: Choose a transcendence basis x of K/k using [lem-exc-transcendence-basis-exists], and put L=k(x). The defining property of the basis says K/L is algebraic. The finite field generators of K/k also generate K/L, so [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] makes K/L finite. In Lean use fg_top_iff, Algebra.EssFiniteType.of_comp, and Algebra.finite_of_essFiniteType_of_isAlgebraic. No finiteness of the indexing set of x is needed.

Put A=algebraicClosure k K [def-weil-relative-algebraic-closure]. Since A/k is algebraic, [lem-zl-independence-algebraic-base] makes x algebraically independent over A. Choose a k-vector-space basis b of A, with arbitrary index type I.

Show that the image of b in K is linearly independent over the polynomial subalgebra R=k[x]. Given a finite relation sum_i c_i b_i=0 with c_i in R, represent each c_i by a polynomial p_i over k using the algebraic-independence equivalence. The polynomial q=sum_i C(b_i) map(p_i) over A evaluates to zero at x. Independence over A gives q=0. For each monomial d its coefficient is sum_i coeff_d(p_i) b_i=0. Independence of b over k forces every coeff_d(p_i)=0, hence every p_i=0 and c_i=0. This is the proved private lemma linearIndependent_adjoin_of_algebraicIndependent, before its localization step.

The field L=k(x) is the fraction field of R=k[x]. A finite linear relation over L can be multiplied by a common nonzero denominator to give one over R; the preceding independence then forces all numerators, and hence all original coefficients, to vanish. Use LinearIndependent.localization and IntermediateField.algebraAdjoinAdjoin.isFractionRing. Thus b stays linearly independent over L in K.

Since K is finite-dimensional over L, the index type I of the L-linearly independent family b is finite (LinearIndependent.finite). The same finite index type indexes the original k-basis of A. Module.Finite.of_basis proves that A/k is finite.
